# Copilot instructions for MySuperApp

## Build, test, and lint commands

### Android

- From the repository root on Windows, use the Gradle wrapper with `-p android` because the Gradle project lives under `android/` while `gradlew.bat` is at the repo root.
- Build the main Android app: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :app:assembleDevRelease`
- Build the QR manager app: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :app-qrcode:assembleDevRelease`
- Run Android unit tests for the main app: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :app:testDevReleaseUnitTest`
- Run a single Android test class: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :app:testDevReleaseUnitTest --tests "com.vfdeginformatica.mysuperapp.data.mapper.AccessLogMapperTest"`
- Run a single Android test method: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :app:testDevReleaseUnitTest --tests "com.vfdeginformatica.mysuperapp.presentation.screen.access_log_map.AccessLogMapViewModelTest.testToggleViewMode"`
- Lint the main Android app: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :app:lintDevRelease`
- Lint the QR manager app: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :app-qrcode:lintDevRelease`
- Compile the NFC feature module: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :feature-nfc:compileDebugKotlin`
- Run unit tests for the NFC feature module: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :feature-nfc:testDebugUnitTest`
- Compile the financial feature module: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :feature-financial:compileDebugKotlin`
- Run unit tests for the financial feature module: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :feature-financial:testDebugUnitTest`
- Compile the workout (gym) feature module: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :feature-workout:compileDebugKotlin`
- Run unit tests for the workout feature module: `.\gradlew.bat -p android :feature-workout:testDebugUnitTest`

### Firebase Functions / web backend

- Install Functions dependencies: `npm --prefix web\functions install`
- Run the Functions emulator: `npm --prefix web\functions run serve`
- Deploy Functions: `npm --prefix web\functions run deploy`
- Read Functions logs: `npm --prefix web\functions run logs`
- Backfill `transactionType` (one-shot migration, Admin SDK credentials required): `npm --prefix web\functions run migrate:transaction-type -- --dry-run` to preview, then `npm --prefix web\functions run migrate:transaction-type` to apply.
- Backfill `userId` (owner) on the financial/gym collections (one-shot, idempotent, only touches documents without `userId`; the UID must exist in the target project's Auth — prd `baila-675c6` and dev `my-super-app-dev-d6819` have different UIDs): `npm --prefix web\functions run migrate:user-id -- --project=<projectId> --uid=<uid> --dry-run` to preview, then without `--dry-run` to apply. Accepts `--collections=`.
- Copy gym catalog/workouts (`exercises`, `workouts`, IDs preserved) from the dev Firebase project to prd (ADC with access to both projects): `npm --prefix web\functions run copy:workout-data -- --target-uid=<prd uid> --dry-run` to preview, then without `--dry-run` to apply. `--target-uid` is required and overwrites `userId` on the copied documents; also accepts `--source=`/`--target=`/`--collections=`.
- Deploy Firestore rules: `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules` (run from `web\`).
- Deploy Firestore composite indexes (`web/firestore.indexes.json`, needed for the `userId`-scoped queries): `firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes` (run from `web\`). Rollout order for the per-user scoping: install the updated app → run `migrate:user-id` → deploy indexes → deploy rules.
- Deploy Storage rules (QR images + authenticated-only `downloader/**` installer/sources): `firebase deploy --only storage` (run from `web\`; Firebase Storage must be enabled in the project console first).
- Publish the local downloader installer + corresponding sources to Storage and write `downloader/latest.json` (prd only, ADC): `npm --prefix web\functions run publish:downloader -- --dry-run` to validate, then without `--dry-run` (`--force` to overwrite a published version, `--notes=a;b` for portal release notes). Run `desktop\downloader\build.ps1` first; then `firebase deploy --only storage,hosting` from `web\`.
- Deploy the web portal + feature-flag rules: `firebase deploy --only hosting,firestore:rules` (run from `web\`).

## High-level architecture

- This is a split Android + Firebase web monorepo. Android code lives in `android/`; the hosted QR page and Firebase backend live in `web/`.
- `android/app` and `android/app-qrcode` are separate Android application modules. Both depend on the shared library modules `android/feature-qrcode` and `android/feature-nfc`; `android/app` additionally depends on `android/feature-financial` and `android/feature-workout`.
- `android/feature-qrcode` contains most QR-specific code: Firebase-backed data sources and repositories, domain models and use cases, and reusable Compose screens such as login, QR detail, QR list, mural comments, and access-log map flows. A `qrcodes/{id}` document has `type` = `REDIRECT` (opens `redirectUrl`) | `TEXT` (shows `text`) | `MURAL` (public comment wall) | `IMAGE` (shows `imageUrl` with `text` as optional caption). `IMAGE` files live in Firebase Storage at `qr_images/{uid}/{qrId}/{timestamp}.jpg` (`web/storage.rules`: public read, owner-only write, `image/*` < 5 MB); the app picks from the gallery with `PickVisualMedia`, downsizes to ≤1600 px JPEG 85% (`data/local/ImageCompressor`), uploads via `QrImageStorageDao`/`QrImageRepository`/`UploadQrImageUseCase`, stores `imageUrl`+`imagePath` on the document and best-effort deletes the previous file (`DeleteQrImageUseCase`) when the image is replaced or the type changes. Creation runs create → upload → update (an upload failure leaves the QR without image and toasts a retry hint). Image previews use Coil (`coil-compose`) through `presentation/components/QrImagePickerField`.
- `android/feature-nfc` contains the NFC tag reading/writing/locking feature: reading and writing NDEF records (URL or custom text), validating tag capacity, and locking a tag permanently (`Ndef.makeReadOnly()`). It has no product flavors, unlike `:app`/`:app-qrcode`.
- `android/feature-financial` contains the finance feature used only by `:app`: the financial home, new-transaction, card (`card_list`/`card_detail`/`new_card`), card-invoice (`card_invoice`, bank-statement view of one card's invoice for a given `yyyy-MM`) and transaction-category (`category_list`/`category_detail`) Compose screens, transaction/card/transaction-category domain repositories and use cases, and Firestore-backed DAOs/DTOs (`TransactionDao`, `CardDao`, `CategoryTransactionDao`). Both `transactions` and `transactions_category` documents carry `transactionType` = `EXPENSE` (despesa) | `INCOME` (receita); missing values are read as `EXPENSE`. It has no product flavors and depends on `:feature-qrcode` for the shared `common.Resource` wrapper and `AppScaffold` composable (a future `:core` module is the natural home for those shared pieces).
- `android/feature-workout` contains the gym feature ("Academia") used only by `:app`: body-measurement history (`body_measurements`, weight/height/date with a Canvas weight chart), an exercise catalog (`exercises`, fixed `MuscleGroup` enum, optional YouTube `videoUrl` played in-app via a `WebView` IFrame embed — `YouTubePlayer`/`YouTubePlayerDialog`, no download) and unlimited user-defined workouts (`workouts`, embedded ordered `items` with optional sets/reps/load/rest). `workouts.exerciseIds` is always derived from `items` so deleting an exercise still referenced by a workout is blocked (`DeleteExerciseUseCase`). Gym visits are logged per workout in `workout_sessions` (date, minutes, calories). Screens: `workout_hub` (Home → Academia: view-mode workout list, collapsible "Outros (N)" group for workouts with `isOther = true`, + highlighted cards "Minha dieta", "Meus dados físicos" → `body_measurement_list`, "Histórico de treinos" → `workout_history`), `workout_history` (session history with a Dias | Semanas switch: last 30 days grouped by day, or a Monday–Sunday week selector up to 12 weeks back with totals, ▲/▼ vs previous week and a bar chart; tap → `workout_view`, delete with confirmation), `workout_view` (workout view: prescription editable per item, no add/remove/reorder, plus session log), `body_measurement_list/detail`, `exercise_list/detail`, `workout_list/detail` (editing, reached from the drawer). Same flavorless setup and `:feature-qrcode` dependency as `feature-financial`; see `.github/instructions/feature-workout.instructions.md`.
- `android/app` is the broader app shell. It adds the main app navigation, home, and biometric authentication, and wires the financial feature module screens (`financial_screen`, `new_transaction_screen`, `card_invoice_screen/{cardId}/{invoiceMonth}`, card and category screens) into its nav graph and drawer ("Controle Financeiro" → Dashboard / Cartões / Categorias). The Home (`presentation/screen/home`) is a `LazyColumn` of three full-width topic cards (`components/HomeTopicCard` + `FinanceTopicCard`/`SmartTagsTopicCard`/`WorkoutTopicCard`, per-topic accent colors in `components/HomeColors.kt`: Finanças teal, Smart Tags blue, Academia orange, light/dark aware) with summaries loaded in parallel by `HomeViewModel` from `GetMonthFinancialSummaryUseCase` (`feature-financial`; balance = income − debit − the card invoices paid in the month, per-card rule in `FinancialTotals.paidInvoiceMonth`, paid amount replacing the projection when a "Pagar fatura" transaction exists), `CountQrCodesUseCase` (`feature-qrcode`) and `GetWorkoutHomeSummaryUseCase` (`feature-workout`); each section has independent loading/error + "Tentar novamente" (`HomeEvent.OnRefresh`). Finanças shows "Saldo do mês"/"Gastos do mês" masked as `••••` until the eye button passes biometrics through the sentinel route `HomeFinanceReveal.ROUTE` (not a NavHost destination; revealed state lives only in the ViewModel) and offers "Adicionar gasto"/"Adicionar receita" chips (`new_transaction_screen/{EXPENSE|INCOME}`). Smart Tags shows the QR count (no biometrics) with "QR Code"/"NFC" chips; the drawer has an expandable "Smart Tags" group (QR Code / NFC subitems). Every Finanças and Smart Tags entry point from the Home and the drawer is biometric-protected via `ResolveProtectedNavigationUseCase` (`passwordRequired = true` / `AppDrawerMenuViewModel.navigateWithBiometric`); the prompt is shown on every entry, not once per session. The "Academia" card (today's workout by `dayOfWeek`, sessions/minutes/kcal of the last 7 days, chips "Treino de hoje" → `workout_view_screen/{id}` and "Minha dieta") and drawer section (Dados físicos / Exercícios / Treinos → `feature-workout` screens) are intentionally **not** biometric-protected. The drawer's "Configurações" item opens `presentation/screen/settings` (`settings_screen`, no biometrics) whose "Notificações" entry opens the shared `NotificationsRoute` (`notifications_screen`). `MainActivity` requests `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`, calls `RegisterFcmTokenUseCase` on resume when logged in, and feeds the notification extra into `PendingQrCodeNavigation`; `NotificationDeepLinkViewModel` (`presentation/my_super_app`) then runs biometrics, loads the QR via `GetQrCodeByIdUseCase` and navigates to its detail (falls back to the QR list with a toast if not found).
- Academia also owns a private daily diet per account (`diets/{uid}`, keyed by uid instead of a `userId` field). Home → Academia → "Minha dieta" (between workouts/history, also shown without workouts) opens strictly read-only `diet_view_screen`; drawer → Academia → Dieta opens `diet_detail_screen` for explicit whole-diet save and confirmed deletion, without biometrics. Ordered meals have optional `HH:mm`/notes and ordered foods with required free-text name/quantity; empty diets/meals are allowed. Diet DAO/repository are wired only in `:app`, observe account changes and prevent saving an old account's draft into another account. Publish the matching private Firestore rules before use; diets are not included in `copy:workout-data`.
- `android/app-qrcode` is a dedicated QR manager shell. It reuses the shared QR feature module (including the FCM service, token registration and Notifications screen) and adds its own nav graph, session flow and profile; `QrCodeManagerNavGraph` consumes `QrCodeDeepLinkViewModel` to open the QR detail from a notification tap.
- The web side is not a bundled frontend app. `web/public/qr/index.html` is a static Firebase Hosting page with inline JavaScript that initializes Firebase directly in the browser.
- **Web portal / feature flags.** `web/public/my-super-app/index.html` (served at `https://mysuperapp.com.br/login` via the `/login` hosting rewrite in `web/firebase.json`; the physical path `/my-super-app/` still works on both domains since `mysuperapp.com.br` and `baila.space` point to the same Hosting site `baila-675c6`; `noindex`) is a static page (compat SDK app/auth/firestore, project `baila-675c6`) with email/password login (same Firebase Auth account as the app) and **Configurações** / **Perfil** sidebar sections. Configurações reads/writes `users/{uid}.featureFlags` — a map of booleans `finance`, `smartTags`, `qrCode`, `nfc`, `workout`, `diet` (missing key = enabled; `web/firestore.rules` `validFeatureFlags()` only allows those keys as bools). Turning a topic off disables its sub-switches in the UI but preserves their values. The Android `:app` honours the flags: shared code lives in `feature-qrcode` (`domain/model/FeatureFlags` with effective getters `isQrCodeEnabled`/`isNfcEnabled`/`isSmartTagsEnabled`/`isDietEnabled`/`hasAnyEnabled`, `data/mapper/FeatureFlagsMapper`, `UserRemoteDao.getFeatureFlags`, DataStore cache `FeatureFlagsLocalStorage` keyed per uid, `FeatureFlagsRepository` with `observe()`/`refresh()`, use cases in `domain/use_case/feature_flags`) and is wired only in `:app` DI. Flags are refreshed on `MainActivity.onResume` and after login (`SessionViewModel`), never realtime; offline/no cache = everything enabled. Disabled topics are hidden on the Home (`HomeViewModel` skips their loads; `HomeEmptyState` when nothing is enabled), in the drawer and in the Academia hub ("Minha dieta"), and blocked for direct navigation by the overlay in `MySuperApp.kt` (`presentation/common/FeatureGate.blockedBy(flags, route)` → `FeatureDisabledScreen`); `NotificationDeepLinkViewModel` refuses QR deep links when `qrCode` is off. `:app-qrcode` ignores the flags.
- **Web profile.** Perfil has independent Dados pessoais and Segurança forms: name-only merge into `users/{uid}.name` (the Android session reads this on next login), read-only Auth email, and password change through `EmailAuthProvider.credential` → `reauthenticateWithCredential` → `updatePassword`. Passwords never go to Firestore or logs, and are cleared on success, section changes and logout. Async profile results are guarded by user identity and session version to avoid rendering a previous account's data. No new backend, Firestore rules or Android changes are needed.
- **Local downloader.** `desktop/downloader` is a Windows x64 Python/Tkinter helper with loopback-only browser UI and bundled yt-dlp/FFmpeg/Deno. It downloads individual YouTube videos as MP3 192 kbps or MP4 (H.264/AAC, maximum 360/720/1080p, merge/remux without video recoding), and finite playlists as sequential MP3 queues with preview, server-held selection and 50-item UI pages. Existing files are skipped, failures do not stop the queue, cancel preserves completed files, and retry targets only failures/cancelled items in the current session. Playlist files have title+video ID without numbering in a safe title+playlist ID subfolder. Build with `.\build.ps1` in that folder (Python 3.12 x64 + Inno Setup 6); test with `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests -v`. The portal's Downloads section opens `mysuperapp-downloader://open` through a top-level `location.assign` (never a hidden iframe, which fires a false-positive `blur`) and treats focus loss / `pagehide` within 2.5 s as "opened" (heuristic; `localStorage.downloaderInstalled` remembers the version), not an HTTP connection to localhost. No Firebase credentials or media files pass through the site. Closing the helper window cancels its Windows Job Object process tree; closing only the browser tab does not. Distribution: `build.ps1` ends by running `collect-sources.ps1` (skip with `-SkipSources`; `-Plan` only prints the component table), which bundles the corresponding source of FFmpeg + every library enabled in `ffmpeg -buildconf` at the commits pinned by the BtbN recipe tag, yt-dlp and Deno into `output\MySuperAppDownloader-<version>-sources.zip` with `SOURCES-MANIFEST.txt`, failing if any source is unresolved. `npm --prefix web\functions run publish:downloader -- [--dry-run] [--force] [--notes=a;b]` (ADC, prd only) uploads installer + sources to Storage `downloader/` and writes `downloader/latest.json` (`version`, `installer`/`sources` `{path,size,sha256,fileName}`, `publishedAt`, `notes`), without public download tokens, and sets the bucket CORS for the portal origins (`--cors-only` does just that; required because successful `?alt=media` responses only carry `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` when the bucket has CORS configured — error responses and preflights do not depend on it); `web/storage.rules` allows `downloader/**` read only for authenticated users. The portal fetches the manifest lazily (once per session, on tab open) via the Storage REST API with `Authorization: Firebase <idToken>`, streams the installer with progress, verifies SHA256 with `crypto.subtle` before saving (mismatch = not saved), hides the installer on non-Windows, and explains the unsigned-binary SmartScreen prompt. After publishing run `firebase deploy --only storage,hosting` in `web\` (see `desktop/downloader/README.md`).
- Firebase Hosting rewrites `/api/log-qr-scan` and `/api/add-mural-comment` to HTTPS Cloud Functions in `web/functions/index.js`.
- QR scan logs and mural comments are stored under Firestore subcollections on `qrcodes/{qrCodeId}`. Firestore-triggered Functions then send FCM notifications to the QR owner, and the Android shared module reads and updates the same QR code, access log, and comment data.
- Push notifications are shared in `android/feature-qrcode` (`com.vfdeginformatica.mysuperapp.notification`): `QrCodeNotificationService` (`@AndroidEntryPoint` `FirebaseMessagingService`, channel `qrcode_notifications`, filters by `users/{uid}.notificationSettings` through `NotificationFilter.shouldShow`, taps open the app launcher activity with `NotificationIntents.EXTRA_QR_CODE_ID`), `PendingQrCodeNavigation` (singleton holding the pending `qrCodeId`), `QrCodeDeepLinkViewModel`, and `requestNotificationPermissionIfNeeded`. Each application module registers the service in its own manifest and declares `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`. Devices are multi-token: `RegisterFcmTokenUseCase` writes `users/{uid}.fcmTokens.{token} = serverTimestamp()` (plus the legacy `fcmToken`) and is called on activity resume **and** by `LoginUseCase` right after a successful login (an in-app logout → login never passes through `onResume`), `UnregisterFcmTokenUseCase` is called by `LogoutUseCase` before sign-out, and `sendToQrOwner` in `web/functions/index.js` multicasts to `fcmTokens` ∪ `fcmToken` via `sendEachForMulticast`, pruning unregistered/invalid tokens. The Notifications toggles screen lives in `feature-qrcode/presentation/screen/notifications` and is reused by both apps.

## Key conventions

- **Receitas culinárias:** `android/feature-recipes` is an independent flavorless module used only by
  `:app`. Home/menu → `recipe_list_screen` (search/favorites) → `recipe_view_screen/{recipeId}`
  (read-only + edit/delete/favorite); Add/Edit → `recipe_detail_screen?recipeId={recipeId}`.
  Recipes live in private per-owner `recipes` documents (`userId` immutable), with ordered ingredients
  and steps, times, yield, category/difficulty, notes and one optional private gallery photo under
  `recipe_images/{uid}/{recipeId}/`. Photos use authenticated Storage reads, not public QR URLs.
  Independent `recipes` flag controls Home, drawer and direct routes; absent = enabled, no biometrics.
  See `.github/instructions/feature-recipes.instructions.md`. Publish Firestore/Storage rules and
  Hosting before use; `npm --prefix web\rules-tests test` validates changed rules with demo emulators.

- The financial dashboard's new-transaction FAB expands into "Gasto" / "Receita" floating actions. Navigate with `Screen.NewTransactionScreen.createRoute(type.name)` (`new_transaction_screen/{transactionType}`); the required argument initializes `NewTransactionViewModel` via `SavedStateHandle`, and the form never allows changing that type. `AppScaffold.floatingActionButtonContent` supports this custom menu while retaining the default FAB on other screens.

- Android feature modules follow the naming convention `feature-<featureName>` (e.g. `feature-qrcode`, `feature-nfc`, `feature-financial`, `feature-workout`). New shared feature modules should be added under `android/feature-<name>` and registered in `android/settings.gradle.kts` with a matching `include(":feature-<name>")`.
- When changing QR-related behavior, check all three Android modules. Shared QR business logic usually belongs in `android/feature-qrcode`, while `android/app` and `android/app-qrcode` only provide app-specific shells, navigation, and DI wiring.
- Android code follows a layered structure across modules: `data/remote` and `data/local` for Firebase/device access, `domain` for models/repositories/use cases, and `presentation` for Compose UI and view models.
- **All user data is per account.** `qrcodes`, the financial collections (`transactions`, `cards`, `transactions_category`) and the gym collections (`body_measurements`, `exercises`, `workouts`, `workout_sessions`) carry a `userId` field; `diets/{uid}` is keyed by uid. Every `*DaoImpl` receives `FirebaseAuth`, writes `userId = auth.currentUser.uid` on create/batch-set and prefixes every query with `whereEqualTo("userId", uid)` (logged-out reads return an empty list, writes fail with a "Entre na sua conta" error). `web/firestore.rules` enforces ownership (`isOwner()`/`createsOwn()`) and keeps `userId` immutable; composite indexes for `userId` + range/array queries live in `web/firestore.indexes.json`. New collections must follow the same pattern (DTO field, DAO filter/write, rule, index, and a `migrate:user-id` entry if backfilling existing data).
- Screen code follows a consistent pattern: `*Route.kt` handles navigation/composition, `*Screen.kt` renders UI, `*ViewModel.kt` owns behavior, and `contract/` packages hold `UiState`, `Event`, and `Effect` types. New screens should match that structure.
- Hilt wiring is app-local. Each Android application module has its own `di/DaoModule.kt`, `RepositoryModule.kt`, `UseCaseModule.kt`, and `UtilModule.kt`, even when they bind implementations from shared feature modules (e.g. `android/app/di` provides the financial DAOs/repositories implemented in `feature-financial`).
- Feature library modules keep the same Kotlin package root (`com.vfdeginformatica.mysuperapp...`) as `:app` even though their Gradle namespaces differ (e.g. `com.vfdeginformatica.feature.financial`). When moving code between modules, preserve packages so app-side imports, DI, and navigation stay unchanged.
- Mapping between Firebase DTOs and domain models is explicit. Reuse the mapper functions in `data/mapper` and the existing `toDto`/`toModel` conversions instead of pushing DTO types into presentation code.
- Android flavors are `dev` and `prd`, and debug build variants are disabled in both application modules. Prefer flavor-aware release tasks such as `assembleDevRelease`, `testDevReleaseUnitTest`, and `lintDevRelease` instead of assuming plain `debug` tasks exist.
- `BuildConfig.IS_DEBUGGABLE` controls Firebase App Check setup. `dev` uses the debug App Check provider and `prd` uses Play Integrity. Preserve that split when touching application startup or comment/scan flows.
- Google Maps API keys are read from `android/local.properties` via `MAPS_API_KEY` and injected through manifest placeholders in both Android application modules. Do not hardcode Maps keys in source files.
- The QR web page is intentionally simple and mostly inline. If you change the hosted QR flow, expect behavior to be driven directly from `web/public/qr/index.html` plus the matching Cloud Functions rather than from a separate JS build system. The page branches on `type`: `REDIRECT` redirects, `TEXT` → `showText`, `IMAGE` → `showImage` (full-width `<img>` + optional `<figcaption>`, tap opens a fullscreen overlay), `MURAL` → comment wall; all non-redirect types log the scan via `trackScanInBackground`.
